purpose: Sanitized source/template contracts derived from the private AturUang source corpus. Raw private documents are evidence only and must not be committed to Git.

rules: SHA-256 is necessary but not sufficient for idempotency.
Use a provider-native/natural document key when available (for example provider + document kind + account identity + statement period, or provider order id).
A same-period semantically identical document can have different bytes; detect semantic duplicates separately.
Preserve archive lineage: parent archive hash, archive depth, and member path in private runtime metadata.
Never use display name alone as account identity.
Do not collapse occurred_at, posted_at, and settlement_date into one date.
Never overwrite raw reference or raw provider transaction id with a normalized value.
Reference is matching evidence, not sole event identity.
A missing running balance is allowed when the source does not print one on every row.
No provider adapter writes directly to the canonical ledger.
A Shopee order is commerce evidence, not proof that the account owner paid.
THIRD_PARTY_DIRECT orders do not create personal expense.
SELF_REIMBURSABLE payments use pass-through/receivable semantics rather than ordinary personal expense.
Category enrichment is applied after payment matching and ownership resolution.
Multi-item orders may allocate shared shipping/fees/discounts using an explicit allocation policy.
Raw financial source files stay outside Git.
Private corpus replay may use a local ignored corpus directory.
Committed tests use sanitized or synthetic fixtures preserving layout/field structure without private values.
Every parser requires both golden fixture tests and private full-corpus replay before release.

edge_cases: posting date can differ from an effective/transaction date embedded in the description
multiline descriptions and references
running balance is not printed on every transaction row
DB/CR semantics are expressed through a mix of row markers and description tokens
Poket lifecycle phrases include initial funding, top-up, move, and scheduled transfer variants
separate fee rows can accompany transfers
PDFs are encrypted but readable without user-entered password in the audited corpus
one April 2026 statement appears semantically identical despite different file bytes
pockets appear/disappear over time and require lifecycle handling
internal pocket-to-pocket moves are owned-to-owned transfers
a pocket display name can collide with another provider name; display name must never be global identity
text extraction contains tabs and wrapped counterparty fields
the phrase TIDAK ADA TRANSAKSI can belong to a deposit section while the main savings section has transactions
zero-transaction detection must be section-scoped
statement generation date is different from transaction coverage period
transaction description and type can occupy separate lines
interest/tax detail pages must not be double-counted as new cash transactions
current August 2026 document is partial/open period
transfers between bluAccount and bluSaving/bluGether are internal
period language/format changes across historical documents
subaccount names require lifecycle tracking
portfolio rows are snapshots and must not be imported as transaction rows
same-period mutation and portfolio documents are complementary evidence, not duplicates
use portfolio documents to discover/close/verify subaccounts and reconcile totals
true zero-transaction monthly statements exist
transaction IDs and descriptions wrap across text lines
a transaction can show more than one payment component such as balance and coins
positive top-up and negative payment/transfer semantics must be preserved raw before classification
image resolution varies dramatically; fixed pixel coordinates are unsafe
long vertical screenshots contain many entries without page boundaries
failed payments must not become successful expense events
refunds must be preserved as refund evidence
image adapter requires quality scoring and fail-closed behavior when extraction confidence is low
trade date and due/settlement date are distinct
invoice rows contain nested buy/sell trade details
receipt/payment cash rows must not be double-counted with trade details
negative balances can be shown in parentheses
portfolio section is optional and absent in at least one audited month
fees and estimated interest have distinct reference semantics
order existence does not prove the account owner paid
the corpus contains multiple recipient/buyer labels and repeated checkout-for-others indicators
24 audited receipts contain a CO Buku line-item label; treat this only as a candidate signal for third-party checkout, never an automatic financial classification
QRIS/payment-method labels are evidence but do not uniquely identify the funding account
same provider label can appear in more than one raw payment-method spelling; preserve raw value before normalization
multi-item and multi-page receipts require line-item parsing
shared shipping, fees, and discounts require explicit allocation if item-level spending categories are reported
